1 شَرَطَ عَلَيْهِ كَذَا , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
شَرِطَ and
شَرُطَ , (S, Msb,) inf. n. شَرْطٌ; (Msb;) and عليه ↓ اشترط كذا; (S, * Msb, * K, * TA;) both signify the same; (S, Msb, K;) [He imposed such a thing as a condition, or by stipulation, upon him;] he made such a thing a condition against him. (TK.) And شَرَطَ عَلَيْهِ فِى البَيْعِ He imposed a thing as obligatory upon him in the sale, and took it upon himself as such. (TK.) ＝
-A2- شَرَطَ, aor.
شَرِطَ and
شَرُطَ , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. شَرْطٌ, (Msb, K,) He (a cupper) scarified; syn. بَزَغَ; (S, K;) as also ↓ شرّط , inf. n. تَشْرِيطٌ. (JK in art. بزغ, and TA. *) [Hence, and from the verb in the sense first mentioned, the saying,] رُبَّ شَرْطِ شَارِطٍ أَوْجَعُ مِنْ شَرْطِ شَارِطٍ [Many a condition of one making a condition is more painful than the scarifying of a scarifier]. (TA.) ―
-b2- He slit the ear of a camel. (TA.) ―
-b3- He slit. and then twisted, [or wove together, (see شَرِيطٌ,)] palm-leaves. (TA.) ＝
-A3- شَرِطَ He fell into a momentous, or formidable, case. (O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
